[NEW:L83]    + ## [5.12.0](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/releases/tag/5.12.0)
[NEW:L84]    + 
[NEW:L85]    + Released on 2026-05-04. All issues associated with this milestone can be found using this [filter](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/milestone/97?closed=1).
[NEW:L86]    + 
[NEW:L87]    + ### Added
[NEW:L88]    + - FreeBSD compilation support.
[NEW:L89]    +   - Added by [Al Hoang](https://github.com/hoanga) in Pull Request [#4029](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4029).
[NEW:L90]    + 
[NEW:L91]    + ### Updated
[NEW:L92]    + - Various CI configurations.
[NEW:L93]    +   - Updated by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L94]    + 
[NEW:L95]    + ### Fixed
[NEW:L96]    + - Rare race in `Request.suspend()` and `Request.cancel()` where the state update would be lost if it occurred before the task was created.
[NEW:L97]    +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L98]    + - `Request.cancel()` incorrectly called `Request.finish()` when the underlying task was already `.completed`.
[NEW:L99]    +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L100]   + - Rare race in `Request.resume()` that could lead to multiple `URLSessionTask`s created.
[NEW:L101]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L102]   + - Repeated calls to `Request.suspend()` and `Request.resume()` could lead to multiple pipeline executions.
[NEW:L103]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L104]   + - Thread-safety issue in `Session.deinit` when accessing internal state.
[NEW:L105]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L106]   + - Rare `Request.finish()` race in `Session.deinit`.
[NEW:L107]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L108]   + - `Session.deinit` called `Request.finish()` on `Request`s that were already finished.
[NEW:L109]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L110]   + - `Request.onHTTPRequest` didn't call the full `Request.cancel()` when the `.cancel` disposition was returned.
[NEW:L111]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L112]   + - Multiple unlikely force unwrap or `unowned self` crashes.
[NEW:L113]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L114]   + - Write to `DataStreamRequest`'s `outputStream` after it was closed.
[NEW:L115]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L116]   + - MIME type parsing, where a single element (`text`) or empty strings would be accepted.
[NEW:L117]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L118]   + - Cancelled `DownloadRequest`s could still trigger retry.
[NEW:L119]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L120]   + - `DataRequest.DataTask` and `DownloadRequest.DownloadTask` could miss early cancellation events if they happened before the underlying `Task` was created.
[NEW:L121]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L122]   + - 🔥 Multiple issues in `AuthenticationInterceptor`. These fixes slightly change the interceptor's behavior.
[NEW:L123]   +     1. `adapt()` enqueued adaptations, leading to requests restarted with a new credential to not execute the whole adapt pipeline again. `AuthenticationInterceptor` will now let those requests fail with the old credential and retry their whole pipeline with the new credential.
[NEW:L124]   +     2. Concurrent adaptations for the same stale credential could trigger multiple refreshes.
[NEW:L125]   +     3. `retry()` now lazily checks for new credentials rather than capturing eagerly.
[NEW:L126]   +   - Fixed by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#4030](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/4030).
[NEW:L127]   +

[NEW:L155]   +

[NEW:L158]   + ### Added
[NEW:L159]   + - Lazy `Request` setup by default. `Request`s are now inert until `resume()`'d, whether automatically or manually. Previous behavior can be restored by using `Session(requestSetup: .eager)`.

[NEW:L162]   +   - Added by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#3996](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/3996).
[NEW:L163]   + - Per-`Request` automatic `resume()` control, with the `shouldAutomaticallyResume` parameter.
[NEW:L164]   +   - Added by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) in Pull Request [#3996](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/3996).
[NEW:L165]   + - `OfflineRetrier`, to retry requests based on `NWPathMonitor` status, as a replacement for `NetworkReachabilityManager`.
[NEW:L166]   +   - Added by [Jon Shier](https://github.com/jshier) and [gourav kumar](https://github.com/gouravkmar) in Pull Request [#3948](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/pull/3948).

[CTX:L15]      ## Asking Questions
[CTX:L16]      
[OLD:L18]    - **We don't use GitHub as a support forum.**
[OLD:L19]    - For any usage questions that are not specific to the project itself, please ask on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com) instead. By doing so, you'll be more likely to quickly solve your problem, and you'll allow anyone else with the same question to find the answer. This also allows maintainers to focus on improving the project for others.
[OLD:L20]    - 
[OLD:L21]    - If you'd like to discuss Alamofire best practices, common usage patterns, ideas for new features, or ongoing development, please use our [Swift Forums](https://forums.swift.org/c/related-projects/alamofire/).
[NEW:L17]    + For any usage questions that are not specific to Alamofire itself (not just HTTP networking in general), discussion of Alamofire best practices, ideas for new features, or ongoing development, please open a [GitHub Discussion](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/discussions).
[CTX:L18]      
[CTX:L19]      ## Reporting Security Issues
[CTX:L20]      
[CTX:L21]      The Alamofire Software Foundation takes security seriously.
[NEW:L22]    + 
[CTX:L23]      If you discover a security issue, please bring it to our attention right away!
[CTX:L24]      
[OLD:L28]    - Please **DO NOT** file a public issue, instead send your report privately to <security@alamofire.org>. This will help ensure that any vulnerabilities that _are_ found can be [disclosed responsibly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsible_disclosure) to any affected parties.
[NEW:L25]    + Please **DO NOT** file a public issue! Instead, send your report privately to <security@alamofire.org>. This will help ensure that any vulnerabilities that _are_ found can be [disclosed responsibly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Responsible_disclosure) to any affected parties.
[CTX:L26]      
[CTX:L27]      ## Reporting Other Issues
[CTX:L28]      
[OLD:L32]    - A great way to contribute to the project is to send a detailed issue when you encounter a problem. We always appreciate a well-written, thorough bug report.
[NEW:L29]    + A great way to contribute to the project is to send a detailed issue when you encounter a problem. We always appreciate a well-written, thorough bug report on [GitHub](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/issues).
[CTX:L30]      
[CTX:L31]      Check that the project issues database doesn't already include that problem or suggestion before submitting an issue. If you find a match, feel free to vote for the issue by adding a reaction. Doing this helps prioritize the most common problems and requests.
[CTX:L32]      
[CTX:L33]      When reporting issues, please fill out our issue template. The information the template asks for will help us review and fix your issue faster.
[CTX:L34]      
[OLD:L38]    - ## Triage Issues [![Open Source Helpers](https://www.codetriage.com/alamofire/alamofire/badges/users.svg)](https://www.codetriage.com/alamofire/alamofire)
[NEW:L35]    + ## Submitting Pull Requests
[CTX:L36]      
[OLD:L40]    - You can triage issues which may include reproducing bug reports or asking for vital information, such as version numbers or reproduction instructions. If you would like to start triaging issues, one easy way to get started is to [subscribe to alamofire on CodeTriage](https://www.codetriage.com/alamofire/alamofire).
[NEW:L37]    + You can contribute by fixing bugs or adding new features. Larger changes MUST be discussed on our [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/discussions) before PR submission, or they may be summarily closed. When submitting a pull request, please add relevant tests and ensure your changes don't break any existing tests (see [Automated Tests](#automated-tests) below).
[CTX:L38]      
[OLD:L42]    - ## Submitting Pull Requests
[NEW:L39]    + ### AI Usage
[NEW:L40]    + 
[NEW:L41]    + All pull requests must disclose the degree to which they were AI tool assisted and PR descriptions should be human written. AI tools may be used to assist in translation, but care should be taken to ensure the AI output remains accurate to the original text and isn't a restyling of it in the AI's voice, lest it be confused with direct AI output.
[CTX:L42]      
[OLD:L44]    - You can contribute by fixing bugs or adding new features. For larger code changes, we recommend first discussing your ideas on our [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/discussions) or [Swift Forums](https://forums.swift.org/c/related-projects/alamofire/). When submitting a pull request, please add relevant tests and ensure your changes don't break any existing tests (see [Automated Tests](#automated-tests) below).
[NEW:L43]    + Failure to disclose AI usage may lead to summary closing of issues and PRs.
[CTX:L44]      
[CTX:L45]      ### Automated Tests
[CTX:L46]      
[CTX:L49]      In your terminal, run the following commands:
[CTX:L50]      - To install Firewalk: `brew install alamofire/alamofire/firewalk`
[CTX:L51]      - To run and detach the server: `firewalk &`
[OLD:L53]    - - To stop the server, run `kill` and provide the pid output after launch.
[NEW:L52]    + - To stop the server, run `killall firewalk` .

Documentation/AdvancedUsage.md   (context only, do not comment)
[CTX:L311]     
[CTX:L312]     `Request`s start in the `.initialized` state after their creation. `Request`s can be suspended, resumed, and cancelled by calling the appropriate lifetime method.
[CTX:L313]     
[OLD:L314]   - - `resume()` resumes, or starts, a `Request`’s network traffic. If `startRequestsImmediately` is `true`, this is called automatically once a response handler has been added to the `Request`.
[NEW:L314]   + - `resume()` resumes, or starts, a `Request`’s network traffic. If `Session.startRequestsImmediately` or `Request.shouldAutomaticallyResume` are `true`, this is called automatically once a response handler has been added to the `Request`.
[CTX:L315]     - `suspend()` suspends, or pauses the `Request` and its network traffic. `Request`s in this state can be resumed, but only `DownloadRequests` may be able continue transferring data. Other `Request`s will start over.
[CTX:L316]     - `cancel()` cancels a `Request`. Once in this state, a `Request` cannot be resumed or suspended. When `cancel()` is called, the `Request`’s `error` property will be set with an `AFError.explicitlyCancelled` instance.
[CTX:L317]       If a `Request` is resumed and isn’t later cancelled, it will reach the `.finished` state once all response validators and response serializers have been run. However, if additional response serializers are added to the `Request` after it has reached the `.finished` state, it will transition back to the `.resumed` state and perform the network request again.

Documentation/Usage.md   (context only, do not comment)
[CTX:L77]      This is actually one form of the two top-level APIs on Alamofire's `Session` type for making requests. Its full definition looks like this:
[CTX:L78]      
[CTX:L79]      ```swift
[OLD:L80]    - open func request<Parameters: Encodable>(_ convertible: URLConvertible,
[OLD:L81]    -                                          method: HTTPMethod = .get,
[OLD:L82]    -                                          parameters: Parameters? = nil,
[OLD:L83]    -                                          encoder: ParameterEncoder = URLEncodedFormParameterEncoder.default,
[OLD:L84]    -                                          headers: HTTPHeaders? = nil,
[OLD:L85]    -                                          interceptor: RequestInterceptor? = nil) -> DataRequest
[NEW:L80]    + open func request<Parameters: Encodable & Sendable>(_ convertible: any URLConvertible,
[NEW:L81]    +                                                     method: HTTPMethod = .get,
[NEW:L82]    +                                                     parameters: Parameters? = nil,
[NEW:L83]    +                                                     encoder: any ParameterEncoder = URLEncodedFormParameterEncoder.default,
[NEW:L84]    +                                                     headers: HTTPHeaders? = nil,
[NEW:L85]    +                                                     interceptor: (any RequestInterceptor)? = nil,
[NEW:L86]    +                                                     shouldAutomaticallyResume: Bool? = nil,
[NEW:L87]    +                                                     requestModifier: RequestModifier? = nil) -> DataRequest
[CTX:L88]      ```
[CTX:L89]      This method creates a `DataRequest` while allowing the composition of requests from individual components, such as the `method` and `headers`, while also allowing per-request `RequestInterceptor`s and `Encodable` parameters.
[CTX:L90]      
[CTX:L93]      The second version of this API is much simpler:
[CTX:L94]      
[CTX:L95]      ```swift
[OLD:L94]    - open func request(_ urlRequest: URLRequestConvertible, 
[OLD:L95]    -                   interceptor: RequestInterceptor? = nil) -> DataRequest
[NEW:L96]    + open func request(_ convertible: any URLRequestConvertible,
[NEW:L97]    +                   interceptor: (any RequestInterceptor)? = nil,
[NEW:L98]    +                   shouldAutomaticallyResume: Bool? = nil) -> DataRequest
[CTX:L99]      ```
[CTX:L100]     
[CTX:L101]     This method creates a `DataRequest` for any type conforming to Alamofire's `URLRequestConvertible` protocol. All of the different parameters from the previous version are encapsulated in that value, which can give rise to very powerful abstractions. This is discussed in our [Advanced Usage](https://github.com/Alamofire/Alamofire/blob/master/Documentation/AdvancedUsage.md) documentation.

[NEW:L743]   +     @MainActor
[NEW:L744]   +     func testThatInterceptorAllowsNewRequestsToTriggerRefreshAfterPreviousRefreshFailure() {
[NEW:L745]   +         // Given
[NEW:L746]   +         // A failed refresh sets .failed state on the interceptor. A subsequent, independent request
[NEW:L747]   +         // that also receives a 401 must be able to trigger a fresh refresh attempt; it is not a
[NEW:L748]   +         // late arrival from the failed batch and must not be permanently blocked by cached failure state.
[NEW:L749]   +         let credential = TestCredential()
[NEW:L750]   +         let authenticator = TestAuthenticator(refreshResult: .failure(TestAuthError.refreshNetworkFailure))
[NEW:L751]   +         let interceptor = AuthenticationInterceptor(authenticator: authenticator, credential: credential)
[NEW:L752]   +         let session = stored(Session())
[NEW:L753]   + 
[NEW:L754]   +         // Phase 1 — first request triggers a refresh that fails.
[NEW:L755]   +         let firstExpect = expectation(description: "first request should complete")
[NEW:L756]   +         var firstResponse: AFDataResponse<Data?>?
[NEW:L757]   + 
[NEW:L758]   +         let firstRequest = session.request(.status(401), interceptor: interceptor).validate().response {
[NEW:L759]   +             firstResponse = $0
[NEW:L760]   +             firstExpect.fulfill()
[NEW:L761]   +         }
[NEW:L762]   + 
[NEW:L763]   +         waitForExpectations(timeout: timeout)
[NEW:L764]   + 
[NEW:L765]   +         // Precondition: first request failed and triggered exactly one refresh.
[NEW:L766]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.applyCount, 1)
[NEW:L767]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.refreshCount, 1)
[NEW:L768]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.didRequestFailDueToAuthErrorCount, 1)
[NEW:L769]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.isRequestAuthenticatedWithCredentialCount, 1)
[NEW:L770]   +         XCTAssertEqual(firstResponse?.result.isFailure, true)
[NEW:L771]   +         XCTAssertEqual(firstRequest.retryCount, 0)
[NEW:L772]   + 
[NEW:L773]   +         // Phase 2 — a new, independent request is made after the failed refresh has fully completed.
[NEW:L774]   +         let secondExpect = expectation(description: "second request should complete")
[NEW:L775]   +         var secondResponse: AFDataResponse<Data?>?
[NEW:L776]   + 
[NEW:L777]   +         let secondRequest = session.request(.status(401), interceptor: interceptor).validate().response {
[NEW:L778]   +             secondResponse = $0
[NEW:L779]   +             secondExpect.fulfill()
[NEW:L780]   +         }
[NEW:L781]   + 
[NEW:L782]   +         waitForExpectations(timeout: timeout)
[NEW:L783]   + 
[NEW:L784]   +         // Then: the new request must trigger its own fresh refresh attempt rather than
[NEW:L785]   +         // immediately failing with the cached error left over from the previous failed refresh.
[NEW:L786]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.applyCount, 2)
[NEW:L787]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.refreshCount, 2) // Fails: .failed state blocks the new refresh, refreshCount stays at 1.
[NEW:L788]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.didRequestFailDueToAuthErrorCount, 2)
[NEW:L789]   +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.isRequestAuthenticatedWithCredentialCount, 2)
[NEW:L790]   +         XCTAssertEqual(secondResponse?.result.isFailure, true)
[NEW:L791]   +         XCTAssertEqual(secondResponse?.result.failure?.asAFError?.isRequestRetryError, true)
[NEW:L792]   +         XCTAssertEqual(secondResponse?.result.failure?.asAFError?.underlyingError as? TestAuthError, .refreshNetworkFailure)
[NEW:L793]   +         XCTAssertEqual(secondRequest.retryCount, 0)
[NEW:L794]   +     }

[NEW:L1431]  +

[NEW:L1433]  +         // and once after retrying with a1 (triggering the excessive check).

[NEW:L1464]  +     @MainActor
[NEW:L1465]  +     func testThatInterceptorAllowsProactiveRefreshFromFailedStateUnlikeRetryPath() {
[NEW:L1466]  +         // Given
[NEW:L1467]  +         // After a proactive refresh failure, refreshState is .failed. The retry path has an explicit .failed case that
[NEW:L1468]  +         // returns .doNotRetryWithError immediately. The proactive adapt path has no such gate. It only checks
[NEW:L1469]  +         // isRefreshing (which is false for .failed), so a new request with requiresRefresh: true triggers another
[NEW:L1470]  +         // proactive refresh, overwriting .failed with .refreshing. This test verifies that asymmetry is intentional
[NEW:L1471]  +         // and preserved.
[NEW:L1472]  +         let credential = TestCredential(requiresRefresh: true)
[NEW:L1473]  +         let authenticator = TestAuthenticator(refreshResult: .failure(TestAuthError.refreshNetworkFailure))
[NEW:L1474]  +         let interceptor = AuthenticationInterceptor(authenticator: authenticator, credential: credential)
[NEW:L1475]  +         let session = stored(Session())
[NEW:L1476]  + 
[NEW:L1477]  +         // Phase 1 — proactive refresh fails, putting interceptor into .failed state.
[NEW:L1478]  +         let firstExpect = expectation(description: "first request should complete")
[NEW:L1479]  +         var firstResponse: AFDataResponse<Data?>?
[NEW:L1480]  + 
[NEW:L1481]  +         session.request(.status(200), interceptor: interceptor).validate().response {
[NEW:L1482]  +             firstResponse = $0
[NEW:L1483]  +             firstExpect.fulfill()
[NEW:L1484]  +         }
[NEW:L1485]  + 
[NEW:L1486]  +         waitForExpectations(timeout: timeout)
[NEW:L1487]  + 
[NEW:L1488]  +         XCTAssertEqual(firstResponse?.result.isFailure, true)
[NEW:L1489]  +         XCTAssertEqual(firstResponse?.result.failure?.asAFError?.isRequestAdaptationError, true)
[NEW:L1490]  +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.refreshCount, 1)
[NEW:L1491]  + 
[NEW:L1492]  +         // Second, a new request with the same requiresRefresh: true credential adapts. It enters the proactive path,
[NEW:L1493]  +         // appends to adaptOperations, calls refresh(), overwriting .failed with .refreshing. The retry path's .failed
[NEW:L1494]  +         // gate is never reached.
[NEW:L1495]  +         let secondExpect = expectation(description: "second request should complete")
[NEW:L1496]  +         var secondResponse: AFDataResponse<Data?>?
[NEW:L1497]  + 
[NEW:L1498]  +         session.request(.status(200), interceptor: interceptor).validate().response {
[NEW:L1499]  +             secondResponse = $0
[NEW:L1500]  +             secondExpect.fulfill()
[NEW:L1501]  +         }
[NEW:L1502]  + 
[NEW:L1503]  +         waitForExpectations(timeout: timeout)
[NEW:L1504]  + 
[NEW:L1505]  +         // Then: a second refresh was triggered (refreshCount == 2), proving .failed did not block the proactive adapt
[NEW:L1506]  +         // path the way it blocks the retry path.
[NEW:L1507]  +         XCTAssertEqual(secondResponse?.result.isFailure, true)
[NEW:L1508]  +         XCTAssertEqual(secondResponse?.result.failure?.asAFError?.isRequestAdaptationError, true)
[NEW:L1509]  +         XCTAssertEqual(secondResponse?.result.failure?.asAFError?.underlyingError as? TestAuthError, .refreshNetworkFailure)
[NEW:L1510]  + 
[NEW:L1511]  +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.applyCount, 0)
[NEW:L1512]  +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.refreshCount, 2)
[NEW:L1513]  +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.didRequestFailDueToAuthErrorCount, 0)
[NEW:L1514]  +         XCTAssertEqual(authenticator.isRequestAuthenticatedWithCredentialCount, 0)
[NEW:L1515]  +     }

[NEW:L574]   +           <div class="section-content top-matter">
[NEW:L575]   +             <h1>RequestSetup</h1>
[NEW:L576]   +               <div class="declaration">
[NEW:L577]   +                 <div class="language">
[NEW:L578]   +                   
[NEW:L579]   +                   <pre class="highlight swift"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">enum</span> <span class="kt">RequestSetup</span></code></pre>
[NEW:L580]   + 
[NEW:L581]   +                 </div>
[NEW:L582]   +               </div>
[NEW:L583]   +             <p>Type describing the timing of <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code> setup after creation.</p>
[NEW:L584]   + 
[NEW:L585]   +           </div>
[NEW:L586]   +         </section>
[NEW:L587]   + 
[NEW:L588]   +         <section class="section">
[NEW:L589]   +           <div class="section-content">
[NEW:L590]   +             <div class="task-group">
[NEW:L591]   +               <ul class="item-container">
[NEW:L592]   +                 <li class="item">
[NEW:L593]   +                   <div>
[NEW:L594]   +                     <code>
[NEW:L595]   +                     <a name="/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO4lazyyA2EmF"></a>
[NEW:L596]   +                     <a name="//apple_ref/swift/Element/lazy" class="dashAnchor"></a>
[NEW:L597]   +                     <a class="token" href="#/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO4lazyyA2EmF">lazy</a>
[NEW:L598]   +                     </code>
[NEW:L599]   +                   </div>
[NEW:L600]   +                   <div class="height-container">
[NEW:L601]   +                     <div class="pointer-container"></div>
[NEW:L602]   +                     <section class="section">
[NEW:L603]   +                       <div class="pointer"></div>
[NEW:L604]   +                       <div class="abstract">
[NEW:L605]   +                         <p>Calls the needed lifetime methods on created <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code>s only after they have <code>resume</code> called. <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code>s are
[NEW:L606]   + inert upon creation.</p>
[NEW:L607]   + 
[NEW:L608]   +                       </div>
[NEW:L609]   +                       <div class="declaration">
[NEW:L610]   +                         <h4>Declaration</h4>
[NEW:L611]   +                         <div class="language">
[NEW:L612]   +                           <p class="aside-title">Swift</p>
[NEW:L613]   +                           <pre class="highlight swift"><code><span class="k">case</span> <span class="kd">lazy</span></code></pre>
[NEW:L614]   + 
[NEW:L615]   +                         </div>
[NEW:L616]   +                       </div>
[NEW:L617]   +                     </section>
[NEW:L618]   +                   </div>
[NEW:L619]   +                 </li>
[NEW:L620]   +                 <li class="item">
[NEW:L621]   +                   <div>
[NEW:L622]   +                     <code>
[NEW:L623]   +                     <a name="/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO5eageryA2EmF"></a>
[NEW:L624]   +                     <a name="//apple_ref/swift/Element/eager" class="dashAnchor"></a>
[NEW:L625]   +                     <a class="token" href="#/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO5eageryA2EmF">eager</a>
[NEW:L626]   +                     </code>
[NEW:L627]   +                   </div>
[NEW:L628]   +                   <div class="height-container">
[NEW:L629]   +                     <div class="pointer-container"></div>
[NEW:L630]   +                     <section class="section">
[NEW:L631]   +                       <div class="pointer"></div>
[NEW:L632]   +                       <div class="abstract">
[NEW:L633]   +                         <p>Calls the needed lifetime methods on created <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code>s immediately upon creation. Default in Alamofire
[NEW:L634]   + versions before 5.11.</p>
[NEW:L635]   + <div class="aside aside-warning">
[NEW:L636]   +     <p class="aside-title">Warning</p>
[NEW:L637]   +     May lead to races between <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html#/s:9Alamofire7RequestC6resumeACXDyF">Request.resume()</a></code> and various lifetime events. Not recommended except
[NEW:L638]   +        for backward compatibility.
[NEW:L639]   + 
[NEW:L640]   + </div>
[NEW:L641]   + 
[NEW:L642]   +                       </div>

[NEW:L573]   +         <section class="section">
[NEW:L574]   +           <div class="section-content top-matter">
[NEW:L575]   +             <h1>RequestSetup</h1>
[NEW:L576]   +               <div class="declaration">
[NEW:L577]   +                 <div class="language">
[NEW:L578]   +                   
[NEW:L579]   +                   <pre class="highlight swift"><code><span class="kd">public</span> <span class="kd">enum</span> <span class="kt">RequestSetup</span></code></pre>
[NEW:L580]   + 
[NEW:L581]   +                 </div>
[NEW:L582]   +               </div>
[NEW:L583]   +             <p>Type describing the timing of <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code> setup after creation.</p>
[NEW:L584]   + 
[NEW:L585]   +           </div>
[NEW:L586]   +         </section>
[NEW:L587]   + 
[NEW:L588]   +         <section class="section">
[NEW:L589]   +           <div class="section-content">
[NEW:L590]   +             <div class="task-group">
[NEW:L591]   +               <ul class="item-container">
[NEW:L592]   +                 <li class="item">
[NEW:L593]   +                   <div>
[NEW:L594]   +                     <code>
[NEW:L595]   +                     <a name="/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO4lazyyA2EmF"></a>
[NEW:L596]   +                     <a name="//apple_ref/swift/Element/lazy" class="dashAnchor"></a>
[NEW:L597]   +                     <a class="token" href="#/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO4lazyyA2EmF">lazy</a>
[NEW:L598]   +                     </code>
[NEW:L599]   +                   </div>
[NEW:L600]   +                   <div class="height-container">
[NEW:L601]   +                     <div class="pointer-container"></div>
[NEW:L602]   +                     <section class="section">
[NEW:L603]   +                       <div class="pointer"></div>
[NEW:L604]   +                       <div class="abstract">
[NEW:L605]   +                         <p>Calls the needed lifetime methods on created <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code>s only after they have <code>resume</code> called. <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code>s are
[NEW:L606]   + inert upon creation.</p>
[NEW:L607]   + 
[NEW:L608]   +                       </div>
[NEW:L609]   +                       <div class="declaration">
[NEW:L610]   +                         <h4>Declaration</h4>
[NEW:L611]   +                         <div class="language">
[NEW:L612]   +                           <p class="aside-title">Swift</p>
[NEW:L613]   +                           <pre class="highlight swift"><code><span class="k">case</span> <span class="kd">lazy</span></code></pre>
[NEW:L614]   + 
[NEW:L615]   +                         </div>
[NEW:L616]   +                       </div>
[NEW:L617]   +                     </section>
[NEW:L618]   +                   </div>
[NEW:L619]   +                 </li>
[NEW:L620]   +                 <li class="item">
[NEW:L621]   +                   <div>
[NEW:L622]   +                     <code>
[NEW:L623]   +                     <a name="/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO5eageryA2EmF"></a>
[NEW:L624]   +                     <a name="//apple_ref/swift/Element/eager" class="dashAnchor"></a>
[NEW:L625]   +                     <a class="token" href="#/s:9Alamofire7SessionC12RequestSetupO5eageryA2EmF">eager</a>
[NEW:L626]   +                     </code>
[NEW:L627]   +                   </div>
[NEW:L628]   +                   <div class="height-container">
[NEW:L629]   +                     <div class="pointer-container"></div>
[NEW:L630]   +                     <section class="section">
[NEW:L631]   +                       <div class="pointer"></div>
[NEW:L632]   +                       <div class="abstract">
[NEW:L633]   +                         <p>Calls the needed lifetime methods on created <code><a href="../../Classes/Request.html">Request</a></code>s immediately upon creation. Default in Alamofire
[NEW:L634]   + versions before 5.11.</p>
[NEW:L635]   + <div class="aside aside-warning">

[CTX:L733]     <p>Once you have your Swift package set up, adding Alamofire as a dependency is as easy as adding it to the <code>dependencies</code> value of your <code>Package.swift</code> or the Package list in Xcode.</p>
